attempt: State a continuation obligation for paragraph sentences or entries that IV.7.2.2 p1 omits, e.g. a different area or condition.
reason: IV.7.3.3 p4 only says sentences or entries needing more than one line may be continued, pointing to Continuation of Lines. IV.7.2.2 p1 says any sentence, entry, phrase or clause may be continued starting subsequent lines in area B: the same permission, wider scope. No condition or exception is added.
quoted: they may be continued on a subsequent line or lines

attempt: State a classification obligation (exactly two entry types) that IV.7.4 p1 omits.
reason: p1 says each Data Division entry begins with a level indicator or a level-number, which is the same two-way split; p2 only names the two types and imposes no further requirement (p4 and p5 carry the per-kind rules).
quoted: begins with a level indicator or a level-number

attempt: Argue the unit is GR (defines a term) or a pure pointer.
reason: It defines a blank line and permits it anywhere in the source program: a relaxation of where lines may appear, which IV.3.1 puts in syntax rules ('relax restrictions'). The trailing pointer sits inside a stating unit.
quoted: A blank line can appear anywhere in the source program

attempt: Argue the kind is GR or the unit is not a row.
reason: A placement restriction on the section header, which IV.3.1 calls an arrangement/restriction rule; no numbered rule states it.
quoted: The section header must start in area A

attempt: Argue the kind is GR, or that a numbered rule restates it.
reason: It gives the order of elements in an entry and requires the last clause to end with a separator period: order of elements, IV.3.1 syntax rule. No numbered rule found that states it.
quoted: The last clause is always terminated by a separator period

attempt: Argue the unit is SR (restricts statements and formats at level 1) or restates VI.1.3.x.
reason: It states the capability scope of Nucleus level 1, which decides what a level-1 implementation provides; the specific syntax limits are in VI.1.3.x units. Scope definition fits a general row; a SR reading is arguable but would still be a row, so the denominator is unaffected.

attempt: Argue the unit is GR or is a lead-in not a row.
reason: It lists the figurative-constant words permitted at each level: a restriction on the words a source program may use (IV.3.1 syntax). The colons introduce inline lists within the sentences, which are the whole content, so no lead-in.
